# Panoramax against our catalog: is there imagery where we actually track?

**Ran:** 2026-09-04, 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-06 ·
**Record:** [`panoramax-feasibility_metrics.json`](panoramax-feasibility_metrics.json) ·
**Generated by:** `scripts/panoramax_feasibility.py` ·
**Issue:** [#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316), phase 1.
Provider context: [`imagery-providers.md`](../imagery-providers.md).

## Verdict

**The gate as [#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) phrases it fails: the median tracked city has no Panoramax imagery at all.**
730 of the 1,144 enabled cities (63.8%) screen to a zero upper bound, which the control group confirms is conclusive, so the catalog median is exactly zero pictures.
Composing the exact zeros with a uniform draw from the rest, an estimated 306 cities (26.8%) hold at least one picture, 118 (10.3%) hold at least 100, and 59 (5.2%) hold at least 1,000 (`catalog_composition` in the record).

**But where Panoramax is present it is not marginal, and in a handful of US cities it is the richest source we have.**
The 20 richest screened cities hold between 15,907 and 1,118,155 pictures each — 3.16 M in total, 1.74 M of them 360° — and 14 of the 20 are in the United States.
Des Moines holds 548,451 360° pictures on Panoramax against 352,570 in Mapillary's census of the identical frozen bbox; Ames holds 135,501 against 83,424.

So the recommendation is the KartaView shape, not the Mapillary shape: **an opt-in channel** ([#248](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/248)) enrolled city by city where the screen says there is something to collect, never a default-membership channel that would spend a nightly slot on the 63.8% of cities known to hold nothing.
The census cost is Mapillary's — the same z14 tiles, a median of 12 per city — with no credential and no per-app quota, so the cost of building it is the collector, not the running.
Whether that collector is worth writing for roughly 20–60 cities is a judgement, not a measurement, and this study stops at the measurement.

## The question

[#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) proposes Panoramax as a fourth provider, and everything about it fits: one federated host, no credential, per-picture metadata richer than any provider we collect, and a vector-tile census that drops onto the seam `census.py` already is.
Exactly one thing decides whether a channel is worth building, and it was unmeasured — **coverage against our largely-US catalog**.
The France/Belgium/Croatia/Taiwan concentration of the platform's ~120 M pictures made "essentially nothing in the cities we track" a real possible outcome, which is why this phase exists before any collector does.

This study measures that and nothing else.
No collector, no scheduler channel, no credential, no write to `data/`.

## Read this before quoting any number below

**Three instruments, and they are not interchangeable.**
The screen produces UPPER BOUNDS over areas much larger than a city; the measure stage produces exact in-bbox counts; the detail stage produces per-picture rows.
A number from one of them is not a number from another, and the record keeps them in separate blocks for that reason.

**A zero screen is conclusive; a positive screen is not.**
Everything below rests on that asymmetry, so it is worth stating plainly.
A screen hexagon is H3 resolution 6 — roughly 36 km² — against a median catalog city of 19.5 km², so a city's screen bound sums hexes far larger than the city sitting inside them.
A positive bound therefore means only "look closer".
A zero bound means the hexes enclosing the city hold nothing at all, which no closer look can contradict — and the controls are the 20 closer looks that checked.

**The stated groups are never pooled.**
`leaders` are the richest screened cities and are the extreme tail by construction; `typical` is a uniform random draw from the screened-positive stratum; `controls` are screened-ZERO cities measured exactly.
One distribution laid over all three would answer none of the three questions they exist to answer.
The only whole-catalog numbers in this writeup are the `catalog_composition` estimates, which compose the strata rather than pool them.

**A truncated city is an estimate, not a census.**
Cities over `--max-tiles-per-city` (200) were sampled in a seeded uniform shuffle of their tiles, and `pictures_scaled_to_bbox` extrapolates from that sample.
Truncation selects exactly the largest cities, so comparing a truncated raw count beside complete ones would understate the tail that decides the question.
The record carries `tiles_probed`, `tiles_total` and `complete` on every row; 9 of the 20 leaders and 6 of the 40 typical cities are truncated.

## Method: three instruments, and why `/search` is not one

[#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) proposed running the federated `/api/search` against a stratified sample of frozen grid bboxes.
Probing the API first — the standing [`provider-access.md`](../provider-access.md) rule — showed that cannot work, and that a strictly better instrument was already there.

### 1. `/api/search` cannot count

It does not paginate.
`links` comes back **empty** at `limit=1`, `limit=1000` and `limit=10000` alike; there is no `next`, and the response carries no `numberMatched`.
`limit=100000` is a hard `400` (`number too large to fit in target type`).

So a bbox holding more pictures than `limit` is indistinguishable from one holding exactly `limit` — which is the one distinction a coverage study is made of.
It is also enormous, because every feature embeds a full ~90-key EXIF blob: 1,000 features is 7.7 MB and 10,000 features is **75 MB**.

Search stays in this study as a bounded METADATA sample — the only place the source instance and the EXIF field of view are available — and never as a census.
The `access` stage below measures its failure modes per city rather than asserting them.

### 2. The map tiles can, and there are two of them

They are different products, not versions of one:

| Endpoint | `grid` layer | `sequences` | `pictures` |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 `/api/map/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt` | z0–z6 only: a **0.1° lattice** of points | z6+ | **z15+** |
| v2 `/api/map/2/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt` | all zooms: **H3 hexagons**, res 3 at z0 → res 6 at z6 → **res 11 at z14** | z15+ | z15+ |

Both `grid` layers carry `nb_pictures`, `nb_360_pictures` and `nb_flat_pictures`; the v2 hexagons add a `date` and a `type`.
The `pictures` layer carries `id`, `ts` (capture), `type`, `account_id` and `first_sequence` per picture.

**The hex counters are whole-hex figures against tile-CLIPPED polygons.** Verified across four adjacent z14 tiles: a hexagon appearing in more than one carries an *identical* `nb_pictures` in each, and 582 features over those four tiles were 483 distinct hexes.
So counters must be deduped by H3 id — summing per tile inflates every hex on a seam — while the geometry must be *unioned* across tiles, since either clipped piece's own centroid sits off-centre and the centre is what decides bbox membership.
The dedupe takes the **maximum** across sightings rather than the first: identical under the verified contract, and if a tile ever carried only its own piece's count, a first-seen zero could write a covered city off as empty, while a maximum is zero only when every piece is.

### 3. The cost ladder over our own frozen grids

Computed offline from `download_common.grid_bbox` over all 1,144 enabled cities, no network:

| Instrument | Zoom | Distinct tiles, whole catalog | Per city p50 / p90 / p95 / max |
|---|---|---|---|
| v2 H3 `grid` — screen | z6 | **113** | 1 / 1 / 1 / 2 |
| v2 H3 `grid` — measure | z14 | 64,650 | 12 / 121 / 240 / 6,480 |
| v1 `pictures` — detail | z15 | 236,808 | 35 / 462 / 900 / 25,418 |

**113 requests screen every city we track.**
That is the whole design: an almost-free stage that can prove absence, then exact measurement spent only where absence was not proven — which makes the gate answerable over the **whole catalog** rather than over the stratified sample #316 asked for.
z14's median of 12 tiles is the Mapillary census median, as it must be: same zoom.

### 4. The control group caught a broken screen

The screen was first built on v1's z6 lattice, which is what the API root's `xyz` link points at.
One control city — screened ZERO, measured exactly — held 2 pictures, which falsifies the one claim the whole design rests on and is precisely what the control group exists to catch.

The cause was neither the margin nor a low-count threshold (the lattice happily reports cells holding a single picture): **the v1 `grid` layer omits populated cells.**
Over three z6 tiles it reported 2.5%, 7.9% and 23.9% fewer pictures than v2's H3 grid over the identical extent, and for the failing city it returned no cell at all where v2 returned one.
A lossy screen is not a slightly worse screen here, it is a broken one, so the screen moved to the v2 H3 grid at the same zoom and the same 113 requests.
H3 resolution 6 is comparable in area to the 0.1° cell it replaces, and a screen hex is selected by **overlap** rather than by centre — a screen hex is often larger than a city bbox, so centre selection would miss the very hex the city sits inside.
The v1 lattice stays reachable as `--screen-variant v1_lattice` so the comparison remains reproducible.

Re-screened on v2, every check available holds: 0 upper-bound violations across the 80 exactly-measured cities, and all 34 cities the v2 screen calls zero that were measured exactly held zero — including 14 that v1 had called positive.
It also rules out **more** of the catalog (730 rather than 607), because v1's lattice-plus-margin was effectively screening a 0.3° neighbourhood.
Since the groups derive from the screen, a corrected screen meant a corrected draw; `--reuse-measured` reused the 23 rows whose tile plan the current settings reproduce exactly rather than re-spending their requests.

### Pacing

30 requests/minute with jittered gaps at CV 0.6, using [#292](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/292)'s shifted-exponential formula imported from `download_common.spaced_gap_seconds` rather than re-derived.
That is roughly half the Mapillary channels' configured rate, against a host with strictly less published guidance — the intended direction of the asymmetry.
`refuse_on_collection_host()` keeps it off makelab\*, and a 403 or 429 ends the run rather than being retried into; neither occurred.
No rate limit is documented anywhere found and no rate-limit headers come back; see [`provider-access.md`](../provider-access.md) for the full access survey.
The whole study spent 113 + 3,321 + 60 + 79 + 3,001 requests over two afternoons, plus a 60-request re-run of the `access` stage on 2026-09-06 once its `datetime` probe was corrected (finding 5).

## Findings

### 1. The screen: 730 of 1,144 cities hold nothing

The upper-bound distribution over all 1,144 enabled cities is p50 0, p75 4.25, p90 1,135, p95 4,381, max 1,430,958 (Paris).
414 cities (36.2%) could not be ruled out, 376 of them in the United States — which is 376 of the 1,100 US cities in the catalog, so the US share not ruled out (34.2%) is the catalog's, not an artifact of the non-US minority.
Every one of the 20 controls — a seeded draw from the 730 — measured zero at z14, in 3,321 requests that also covered the other two groups.

### 2. A typical city that is not ruled out holds a handful of pictures

The `typical` group is a uniform draw of 40 from the 394 screened-positive cities that are not leaders.
29 of the 40 held at least one picture; the distribution is p50 3, p75 83, p90 977, p95 1,828, max 9,540 (Port Angeles, 9,529 of them 360°).
10 of the 40 held 100 or more, 4 held 1,000 or more, and none held 10,000.

Scaled to the stratum that is what the composition says: an estimated 118 catalog cities at 100 or more pictures, 59 at 1,000 or more.
At 10,000 or more the estimate is exactly the 20 measured leaders, which is a **floor** — 0 of 40 in the draw bounds the stratum's share at roughly 7% at 95% confidence, so up to a couple of dozen unmeasured cities could sit above that line.

### 3. Where Panoramax is present, it is the richest source in several US cities

The 20 leaders, in-bbox pictures off the z14 grid, with Mapillary's census of the same frozen bbox beside them where one exists.
Panoramax figures are exact for complete cities and `pictures_scaled_to_bbox` estimates for truncated ones (marked ~); the 360° column is the sampled count and is not scaled.
Mapillary figures are `unique_panos` (360°) and `num_flat_images` from the published aggregate `cities.json.gz` (schema v3, generated 2026-09-04), each from that city's latest Mapillary run; GSV is that city's latest grid coverage from the same aggregate.

| City | Panoramax pictures | of which 360° | Mapillary 360° | Mapillary flat | GSV coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paris, France | 1,118,155 | 355,278 | — | — | 89.2% |
| Des Moines, IA | 551,060 | 548,451 | 352,570 | 89,322 | 57.5% |
| Amsterdam, NL | ~418,633 | 335,798 | 1,002,731 | — | 51.7% |
| Tulsa, OK | ~273,763 | 0 | — | — | 40.0% |
| Kansas City, MO | ~203,285 | 53,798 | — | — | 62.9% |
| Taipei, Taiwan | 162,292 | 71,619 | — | — | 52.0% |
| Oklahoma City, OK | ~148,119 | 40,804 | 87,427 | 75,400 | 38.5% |
| Ames, IA | 141,914 | 135,501 | 83,424 | — | 34.4% |
| Zurich, Switzerland | 120,016 | 8,923 | 76,082 | 1,975,799 | 56.0% |
| Toronto, Canada | ~118,477 | 43,926 | — | — | 56.4% |
| Lincoln, NE | 101,966 | 947 | 167,757 | 256,085 | 46.2% |
| Omaha, NE | ~96,424 | 27,800 | 83,034 | 255,421 | 51.1% |
| Madison, WI | 70,520 | 51,092 | — | — | 45.2% |
| Zaragoza, Spain | ~57,265 | 1 | — | — | 30.6% |

| Cuenca, Ecuador | ~43,715 | 36,427 | 40,168 | 130,969 | 5.6% |
| Saint Paul, MN | 36,555 | 1,398 | — | — | 77.9% |

| Bremerton, WA | 20,197 | 10,175 | 3,018 | 43,693 | 28.7% |

Three things to read off it.
**The US cluster is the upper Midwest** — Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas, Missouri, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Oklahoma — and the `instances` stage attributes nearly all of it to a few contributors uploading to the OSM-FR instance, with the Pacific Northwest (Boise, Newberg, Port Angeles) on the `panoramax-us-nw` instance.
**The 360° share is a per-city property**, from 99.5% in Des Moines to 0% in Tulsa and Boise, exactly as [#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) said of Zagreb; a collector reports both numbers under [#116](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/116) or it misdescribes half the leaders.
**Panoramax exceeds Mapillary's 360° census in Des Moines, Ames and Bremerton**, matches it in Boise and Cuenca, and trails it everywhere else — so it is a genuine second source in a few cities, not a proxy for Mapillary anywhere.

### 4. "Field of view absent" is a search artifact: those pictures are flat

[#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) read the 10–34% of search results carrying no `pers:interior_orientation.field_of_view` as a third imagery state.
The `instances` stage sampled 8,020 pictures through `/api/search` over the 20 detail cities (14 of them at the 500 cap), classified each by its search field of view, then looked the same picture ids up in the z15 `pictures` layer, whose `type` field has no absent state — the federation-wide z0 totals sum to 119.4 M pictures with 0 unclassified.

| Search field of view | Tile `type` | Pictures |
|---|---|---|
| 360 | `equirectangular` | 2,723 |
| flat | `flat` | 1,446 |
| **absent** | **`flat`** | **2,136** |
| 360 | not in the fetched tiles | 951 |
| absent | not in the fetched tiles | 764 |

**Every one of the 2,136 EXIF-less search pictures that could be looked up is `flat` in the tiles, and there is not one contradiction in the other two classes.**
"Absent" is 36.2% of the search sample — 100% of it in Boise, North Adams, Watertown, New Hope, Ridgeley, Pierre and Aberdeen — and it is a property of the search endpoint's EXIF passthrough, not of the imagery.
A collector built on the tile `type` never sees the state; one built on search and using `filter=field_of_view=360` discards nothing it should keep, but one that counted "absent" as unknown-possibly-360 would overstate 360° coverage in every one of those cities.
The India comment on [#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) therefore reads as "flat or nothing", which is what it already concluded.

### 5. The three search behaviours phase 2 must design around, measured

The `access` stage sent three searches per detail city — a baseline at `limit=300`, the same with a `datetime` window, and the same with `filter=field_of_view=360` — and derived each finding from the responses.

| Behaviour | Cities that can answer | Cities that showed it |
|---|---|---|
| Search reports no `next` link and no `numberMatched` | 20 (always answerable) | 20 |
| The `datetime` window returns pictures from outside it | 20 | 20 |
| `filter=field_of_view=360` returns no EXIF-less picture | 17 | 17 |

**Two of the three carry a denominator, because a city can fail to be evidence either way.**
A city whose baseline sample held no EXIF-less picture cannot show the field-of-view filter dropping one; three of the twenty are in that position and the record counts them out rather than either way.

The `datetime` probe needs the same guard for the same reason, and getting it wrong is what the window being **derived per city** now prevents.
The window was originally the fixed `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z/..`, justified as being in the future relative to the imagery — which it stopped being eight months before this study ran.
In a city whose imagery lies entirely inside the window an honoured filter returns exactly what an ignored one returns, so the probe read "ignored" whichever was true: Boise's 300 baseline rows span 27 hours in 2026-08, and it was counted among the twenty while being no evidence at all.
Asking instead for "at or after this city's own newest capture" leaves something to drop wherever a baseline holds two distinct timestamps, which is every one of the twenty — Boise included, where the derived window `2026-08-27T21:27:43Z/..` excludes 299 of its own 300 baseline rows.

The re-run on 2026-09-06 is what the table above reports, and the finding came back stronger rather than merely better-founded.
**Across the twenty cities the requested windows should have excluded 5,045 baseline pictures, and all 5,045 came back** — Amsterdam's window `2025-07-14T06:55:26Z/..` returned all 300 of its rows, 299 of them older than the window's own start.
Not one city dropped one picture.

The datetime one is the dangerous one for a collector: an incremental "everything since the last run" fetch would silently re-read the whole history and report it as new.

### 6. Dates and contributors: recent, and one or two people per city

The `detail` stage read 1,345,143 pictures off the z15 `pictures` layer over the 20 detail cities — the 12 richest, each sampled at 200 tiles, plus the 8 cross-check cities read completely — in 3,001 requests.
**Not one of the 1,345,143 carried an absent `type`, and not one was undated**, which is finding 4 restated per picture rather than per total.

Capture months per city run p50 7.5, p75 29, max 130 (Paris, back to 2015 with a two-picture 1970 epoch sentinel; see caveats).
The US leaders are new: Des Moines spans 2023-07 to 2026-04 in 26 months, Ames 2023-04 to 2026-04, Lincoln 2025-04 to 2026-03 in 10 months, Kansas City 5 months in 2024–25, and Boise's entire 54,592-picture deployment is **three months old** (2026-07 to 2026-09).
So a Panoramax series in these cities would start with a short history and, unlike GSV, no archive to backfill — the temporal question this project asks needs the nightly channel to be there when the imagery lands.

Contributor concentration is the other property that decides what a series would mean.
The top contributor's share is p50 0.89 and p75 1.0: 9 of the 20 cities are one account, Lincoln's 32,806 pictures included, and Des Moines and Ames are 3 accounts each.
That is the same shape [#316](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/316) saw in Seattle, and it means a city's Panoramax coverage is a person's project — a change in it is a diff in one contributor's habits, not in a platform's deployment — which is worth saying in any frontend label before a reader compares it with Google's driving plan.


### 7. The two tile instruments agree

The z14 grid's counters are aggregated by the server; the z15 `pictures` layer is a row per picture that this script counts itself, and nothing else in the study checks the aggregate layer every count rests on.
Over the 8 cities complete in both stages — the `--cross-check-cities` set, since none of the 12 richest fits under 200 z15 tiles — the z15-to-z14 ratio is p50 1.000, min 0.9989, max 1.0357.
Five cities agree exactly (Watertown 451, New Hope 249, North Adams 560, Pierre 7, Aberdeen 3); the other three differ by 1 to 3 pictures on the z15 side (Rye 280 vs 277, Ridgeley 29 vs 28, Newberg 940 vs 941), which is a picture on a hexagon edge assigned differently by the two geometries.
The hex counters mean what the study takes them to mean.


### 8. The federation, on the day

23 registered instances, 119,769,867 pictures, 2,580 contributors and 1,094,397 km of sequences (`/api/stats`, which the API root does not advertise).
IGN holds 57.98 M and OSM-FR 53.71 M; then OSM-HR 4.24 M, OSM-TW 1.25 M, OSM-BE 0.65 M, a private Austrian instance 0.60 M, a Dutch test instance 0.36 M and `panoramax-us-nw` 0.26 M.
Of the 8,020 sampled pictures over our cities, 4,927 came through OSM-FR and 1,000 through `panoramax-us-nw`; only 339 came from IGN, whose 58 M pictures are France.
So for our catalog the federation is effectively one volunteer-run instance plus a regional US one, which argues for the conservative end of any pacing range rather than against it.

## What this justifies

- **No default-membership `panoramax` channel.** 63.8% of the catalog is known to hold nothing, and a nightly slot spent confirming that is a slot taken from a city with a second dated interval to gain ([#308](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/308)).
- **An opt-in channel is defensible for the leaders**, on the KartaView pattern ([#248](https://github.com/jonfroehlich/streetscape-tracker/issues/248)): enrolled per city, the screen (113 requests, whole catalog) as the enrolment test, and both coverage numbers reported.
  Whether the collector is worth writing for a few dozen cities is the decision this study hands back.
- **The collector, if built, is the tile census** — z14 v2 H3 grid for counts, z15 `pictures` for per-picture rows — never `/api/search`, and never an incremental `datetime` fetch.
  `type` is two-state; nothing needs a third bucket.
- **The screen is the cheap re-check.** 113 requests re-screen the whole catalog, so "has Panoramax reached city X yet" is answerable any afternoon without re-running anything else.

## Caveats

**A hex is assigned to a city by its centre in the measure stage, not clipped to the bbox.**
A res-11 hexagon is about 2,150 m² — roughly 25 m across — against city bboxes measured in kilometres, so the error is tens of metres at the boundary of a rectangle whose own edges are a modelling choice.
The screen selects by overlap instead, because a res-6 hex is often larger than the city.

**The composition estimates rest on a draw of 40.**
Shares from `typical` carry the sampling error of n = 40 uniform draws from 394; the zero stratum and the leaders carry none.
The at-or-above-10,000 estimate in particular is a floor, as finding 2 says.

**The Mapillary comparison is between two censuses with different collectors and dates.**
Mapillary's `unique_panos` counts 360° images its tile census found in the bbox on that run's date; Panoramax's are the z14 grid counters on 2026-09-04/05.
Both are in-bbox picture counts, so the direction of the comparison is sound; the ratio is not to two decimals.

**The instances stage is a sample capped by `--search-limit`, and can never be a count.**
Its instance shares describe whichever pictures the unpaginated search returned first, and 14 of 20 cities were at the cap.

**Nothing here measures sustained load.**
This is one session on one laptop IP against a host that publishes no limit, and it is not evidence about what a nightly channel could sustain.
Per the standing rule that question gets *asked* on the Panoramax forum before a collector exists, not inferred from a study that did not stress anything.

**Two Paris pictures are dated 1970-01.**
That is the Unix epoch, not a capture date, and the tile `ts` carries it verbatim; a collector reads capture dates through `analysis.dated_unique_panos`' provider floor like every other provider's, and this is Panoramax's first known sentinel.
The other 1,345,141 pictures seen carry plausible dates.

**Coverage is a moving target on a growing platform.**
Panoramax gained instances and pictures throughout 2026 — the newest hex date in Paris, Boise and Denver is within days of the run — so these numbers date quickly in the upward direction.
A re-run is 113 requests for the screen; that is the number to re-check before treating any verdict here as still current.

## Replicating

```bash
python scripts/panoramax_feasibility.py --stage screen        # 113 requests, whole catalog
python scripts/panoramax_feasibility.py --stage measure       # the three groups, ~3,300 requests
python scripts/panoramax_feasibility.py --stage access        # 3 searches per detail city
python scripts/panoramax_feasibility.py --stage instances     # bounded search sample + reconciliation
python scripts/panoramax_feasibility.py --stage detail        # per-picture rows, ~3,000 requests
python scripts/panoramax_feasibility.py --analyze --docs-dir docs/experiments
```

Each stage writes its raw output to the gitignored `experiments/panoramax-feasibility/`, and `--analyze` is the **sole producer** of `docs/experiments/panoramax-feasibility_metrics.json` — it reads only those raw files, makes no request, and can be re-run offline to reproduce the record.
`--stage measure` reads the screen's output to pick its groups, and `detail`, `instances` and `access` all read the measure stage's, so the order above is the dependency order; `--city` overrides any selection and is stamped when used.
An unknown `--city` id, or any invocation that resolves to no cities, exits **64** having fetched and written nothing — a stage writes its artifact unconditionally when it finishes, so a zero-city run is not a no-op but a successful-looking overwrite of the last real one.
Every stage has `--dry-run`, which plans and prices it without a request.

Each city-walking stage also checkpoints after every city into `<stage>.partial.json` beside its artifact, so a run killed part way through costs one city rather than the whole afternoon; the canonical `<stage>.json` is only ever replaced by a run that finished, and a leftover `.partial.json` always means one that did not.

Load-bearing flags: `--seed` (the group draws and every tile shuffle), `--max-tiles-per-city` (which cities end up truncated, and which fit the cross-check), `--leaders`/`--typical`/`--controls` (the group sizes), `--detail-cities`/`--cross-check-cities` (the detail set), `--screen-variant` (v2 by default; v1 only for the comparison) and `--search-limit` (the only thing bounding the instances sample).
All of them are stamped into `_about.measured_by` when they differ from their defaults, so the record names the run that produced it.
`--catalog-label` records *which* catalog without putting a machine's directory layout in a committed file.
